node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Mean total sum
node.description: Find or interpret the total sum of all data values when calculating or reasoning about the mean.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Mean number of values
node.description: Use the count of data values as the divisor when calculating the mean.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Mean from frequency table
node.description: Calculate the mean from a frequency table by multiplying each value by its frequency before dividing by the total frequency.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Weighted mean introduction
node.description: Interpret a weighted mean as a mean where values contribute according to different frequencies or weights.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Median with odd number of values
node.description: Find the single middle value of an ordered data set with an odd number of values.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Median with even number of values
node.description: Find the median of an ordered data set with an even number of values by averaging the two middle values.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Multiple modes or no mode
node.description: Recognise that a data set may have one mode, more than one mode, or no mode when no value repeats most often.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Mode for categorical data
node.description: Use the mode to identify the most frequent category when data are categorical rather than numerical.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Range calculation
node.description: Calculate range by subtracting the minimum value from the maximum value.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Lower and upper quartiles
node.description: Identify lower and upper quartiles as values that mark the lower and upper quarters of an ordered data set.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: IQR calculation
node.description: Calculate the interquartile range by subtracting the lower quartile from the upper quartile.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Five-number summary order
node.description: List minimum, lower quartile, median, upper quartile and maximum in the correct order for a five-number summary.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Outlier gap detection
node.description: Identify possible outliers by looking for values separated from the main cluster of data.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: IQR outlier rule introduction
node.description: Use the 1.5 times IQR rule as an introductory method for flagging possible outliers.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Resistant measure introduction
node.description: Describe a resistant summary measure as one that is not strongly affected by extreme values.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Median resistant to outliers
node.description: Explain why the median is usually less affected by extreme values than the mean.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Mean sensitive to outliers
node.description: Explain how a very large or very small value can pull the mean away from the main cluster of data.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Mean absolute deviation introduction
node.description: Interpret mean absolute deviation as the average distance of data values from the mean.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Variance introduction
node.description: Interpret variance as an average squared deviation from the mean for a numerical data set.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Standard deviation introduction
node.description: Interpret standard deviation as a typical distance of data values from the mean, in the original units of the data.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Units of summary statistics
node.description: State the units of a summary statistic and distinguish unitless counts from measurements with units.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Rounding summary statistics
node.description: Round summary statistics to a precision appropriate for the data and context.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Same centre different spread
node.description: Recognise that two distributions can have similar centres but different variability.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Same spread different centre
node.description: Recognise that two distributions can have similar variability but different centres.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Group comparison overlap
node.description: Compare distributions by considering overlap between groups as well as differences in centre and spread.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Practical difference introduction
node.description: Judge whether a difference between group summaries is large enough to matter in context, not merely whether numbers differ.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Summary claim in context
node.description: Write a statistical comparison claim that names the groups, variable, summary measure and context.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Mean uses all values
node.description: The mean depends on every data value because it uses the total sum and the number of values.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Even median averages middle pair
node.description: When an ordered data set has an even number of values, the median is the average of the two middle values.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: IQR equals Q3 minus Q1
node.description: The interquartile range is calculated by subtracting the lower quartile from the upper quartile.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Median is resistant
node.description: The median is usually resistant to extreme values because it depends on position in ordered data, not the size of every value.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Standard deviation uses original units
node.description: Standard deviation is expressed in the original units of the data, unlike variance, which uses squared units.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Median found without ordering
node.description: Learner chooses the middle entry in the recorded list instead of first ordering the data values.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Range is largest value
node.description: Learner reports the maximum value as the range instead of subtracting minimum from maximum.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: IQR uses min and max
node.description: Learner calculates interquartile range from maximum minus minimum instead of upper quartile minus lower quartile.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Standard deviation is range
node.description: Learner interprets standard deviation as the whole distance between smallest and largest values rather than typical distance from the mean.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Different means imply important difference
node.description: Learner treats any difference in means as meaningful without considering spread, overlap, sample size or context.

edge.rationale: Calculating a mean necessarily practises finding or using the data total.
The even-number case is a core part of median calculation practice.
IQR calculation directly practises interquartile range.
Gap detection is a common first method for identifying possible outliers in context.
Considering overlap is central to comparing distributions responsibly.
The mean is calculated for numerical data, not nominal categories.
edge.failure_signal: Learner tries to average category labels or non-numerical responses.

edge.rationale: Mean calculation uses both the total sum and the number of values.
edge.failure_signal: Learner divides by the wrong count or ignores repeated values.

edge.rationale: Frequency-table means extend mean calculation by using frequencies as repeated counts.
edge.failure_signal: Learner averages distinct values without weighting by frequency.

edge.rationale: Weighted mean builds on the idea that values can contribute more than once or with different weights.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats all weighted categories as equally important.

edge.rationale: The odd-number case depends on ordering data before locating the middle value.
edge.failure_signal: Learner selects the middle recorded entry without ordering.

edge.rationale: The even-number case extends middle-value reasoning to a middle pair.
edge.failure_signal: Learner chooses one of the two middle values rather than averaging them.

edge.rationale: Recognising multiple or no modes depends on knowing mode as the most frequent value.
edge.failure_signal: Learner forces every data set to have exactly one mode.

edge.rationale: Mode is the centre measure that can naturally apply to categorical data.
edge.failure_signal: Learner tries to calculate a mean for nominal categories instead of using the most frequent category.

edge.rationale: Range calculation requires identifying smallest and largest values, which is supported by ordering data.
edge.failure_signal: Learner reports the maximum value or subtracts in the wrong direction.

edge.rationale: Quartiles extend ordered-data and median reasoning to lower and upper halves.
edge.failure_signal: Learner finds quartiles without ordering or splits the data inconsistently.

edge.rationale: IQR calculation requires first identifying lower and upper quartiles.
edge.failure_signal: Learner subtracts minimum from maximum instead of lower quartile from upper quartile.

edge.rationale: A five-number summary uses quartile values and extremes in a fixed order.
edge.failure_signal: Learner swaps quartiles or omits median/minimum/maximum.

edge.rationale: Gap-based outlier detection builds on visually identifying clusters, gaps and outliers in displays.
edge.failure_signal: Learner calls any large value an outlier without comparing it with the distribution pattern.

edge.rationale: The 1.5 IQR rule requires first calculating the IQR.
edge.failure_signal: Learner applies the rule using range or quartile values incorrectly.

edge.rationale: Resistance is understood by comparing how measures respond to outliers.
edge.failure_signal: Learner assumes all centre measures are affected equally by extreme values.

edge.rationale: Median resistance is a key example of a resistant measure.
edge.failure_signal: Learner thinks an extreme value changes the median as much as it changes the mean.

edge.rationale: Mean sensitivity is one of the main effects of outliers on centre.
edge.failure_signal: Learner chooses the mean for a skewed data set with extreme values without checking suitability.

edge.rationale: MAD is calculated from distances between values and the mean.
edge.failure_signal: Learner averages signed deviations and gets zero rather than a measure of spread.

edge.rationale: Variance is based on squared deviations from the mean.
edge.failure_signal: Learner calculates spread without reference to deviations from a centre.

edge.rationale: Standard deviation is the square root of variance and returns spread to original units.
edge.failure_signal: Learner interprets variance and standard deviation as interchangeable units.

edge.rationale: Interpreting summaries in context includes naming relevant units.
edge.failure_signal: Learner reports a summary statistic without units or uses the wrong units.

edge.rationale: Rounding decisions depend on the measurement unit and context of the data.
edge.failure_signal: Learner reports too many decimals or rounds away meaningful precision.

edge.rationale: Recognising same-centre/different-spread cases requires comparing spread while holding centre roughly constant.
edge.failure_signal: Learner says two groups are similar because their centres match despite very different variability.

edge.rationale: Recognising same-spread/different-centre cases requires comparing centres while spread is similar.
edge.failure_signal: Learner says two groups are similar because their spread matches despite shifted centres.

edge.rationale: Overlap comparisons build on reasoning about centre and spread together.
edge.failure_signal: Learner compares only one summary number and ignores how much the distributions overlap.

edge.rationale: Practical difference judgments consider whether group differences are large relative to spread and overlap.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats any nonzero difference in means or medians as important.

edge.rationale: A contextual comparison claim should account for the practical size of differences between groups.
edge.failure_signal: Learner makes a vague claim without groups, variable, summary measure or context.
